subject: On-prem Kubernetes: NIC bonding, node-class matrix, and PV protection
messages:
From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@rivertonhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem Kubernetes: NIC bonding, node-class matrix, and PV protection

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the intake call yesterday. Per our chat I put together a concise operational proposal focused on three risk areas you flagged: network bonding/egress, node-class segmentation, and persistent-volume (PV) protection for model artifacts and customer data. Attachments: riverton-nodeclass-matrix.xlsx (workbook), site-intake-checklist.pdf (preflight).

High-level recommendations (summary):
- Control plane: 3 controllers (HA) running etcd as a dedicated 3-node quorum. Each controller: 2x10Gb NICs in LACP (bond0), MTU 9000 where the switch supports it.
- Worker node classes:
  - model-inference (GPU-capable): 8xA100-style GPUs or equivalent; local NVMe for KV/cache; blockstore mount for checkpoints.
  - batch-train (cpu-heavy): large memory, high-core; ephemeral NVMe OK.
  - system+ingress: small footprint nodes with fast egress to private peering.
- Network topology suggestions: dual-homed racks with LACP aggregation for cross-rack failover; optional BGP peer for egress path (we can fall back to static routing for a simpler setup).
- Storage & PV strategy:
  - Two classes of storage: fast-local NVMe (ephemeral + local PVs for cache / KV) and replicated blockstore (Ceph/Rook or customer-managed SAN) for checkpoints and long-term artifacts.
  - Use CSI snapshots + regular object-store backups (S3-compatible gateway) for model artifacts. Snapshot cadence: hourly for checkpoints, daily for retained artifacts.
  - PV retention policy & recovery: retain snapshots for 90 days by default; provide an export path to your S3 archive for ≥1 year retention if regulated.
- Encryption & keys: encrypt at-rest via CSI + KMS. We support BYO-KMS/HSM — recommended for PHI-sensitive workloads.
- Node lifecycle & maintenance: drain-by-default with preStop hooks for in-flight inference; liveness/readiness tuned to 20s initial probe for heavy models; cordon/drain automation in maintenance windows.
- Failure & rollback: automatic fallback route to a lower-capacity model variant in hosted fallback if on-prem suffers a zone failure; internally, we recommend staging a read-only fallback of last-known-good artifacts to an object-store gateway.

Open questions for you (please provide before the workshop):
1) Rack-level topology / crossconnect details (switch models, support for MLAG/LACP, support for jumbo frames)
2) Expected steady-state RPS and 95th percentile latency SLOs (per model) so we can size caching correctly
3) KMS preference: BYO-HSM vs cloud KMS (we'll need certs and network routes for BYO)
4) Procurement timeline / SOW requirements (Procurement contact cc'ed)

Proposed next step: 60–90 minute onsite/remote workshop to walk the node-class matrix and run a quick failure-mode tabletop for PV restorations. I dropped a meeting placeholder (see related links).

Attached: riverton-nodeclass-matrix.xlsx (draft), site-intake-checklist.pdf (preflight), blockstore-io-diagram.png

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@rivertonhealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@rivertonhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem Kubernetes: NIC bonding, node-class matrix, and PV protection

Diego —

Appreciate the concise plan. A few clarifying items before we schedule the workshop:
1) We are required to run control-plane across three racks for physical separation. Is your recommendation still 3 controllers if they're cross-rack?
2) For NVMe local PVs used as cache, who owns cleanup/eviction behavior? We can enforce retention on object-store, but local disk reclamation is a procedural gap for us.
3) Procurement is asking for a high-level SOW and a list of evidence we will need for our internal auditors (SOC2 / HIPAA scoping). Can you flag the minimal items so our compliance team can start early?

Also — what is the expectation for on-call during the first 30 days after cutover (we may want Redwood to provide an elevated runbook).

Available times for the workshop next week: Tue 15 Jun 10:00–12:00 PDT or Wed 16 Jun 13:00–16:00 PDT.

Thanks,
Alex Jenkins
VP Product & Engineering
Riverton Health
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem Kubernetes: NIC bonding, node-class matrix, and PV protection

Diego / Irene —

Quick internal notes before we reply to Alex:
- I agree on 3 controllers. Cross-rack is fine; we'll call out quorum placement and require symmetric latency under 2ms.
- Local NVMe eviction: recommend we ship a small operator (we've used a lightweight reclaim-controller) that enforces eviction policy by label (cache=true) and reports metrics to Console. We should include that in SOW.
- Compliance evidence: provide a table (we'll author) listing SOC2 artifacts relevant to on-prem: penetration test summaries, encryption config, KMS attestation, network segmentation diagrams, and signed SOW/manifest of data flows.
- On-call: propose a 30-day elevated support window (Mon-Fri 8–18) with 1-hour P1 SLA for cutover period; add as an optional line item on SOW.

I'll draft the SOW bullets and attach to the reply.

—Marissa
Director, Solutions Delivery
From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@rivertonhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@rivertonhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem Kubernetes: NIC bonding, node-class matrix, and PV protection

Alex / procurement team —

Thanks for the questions — answers and next steps below.

1) Controllers & topology: 3 controllers cross-rack is our recommended HA posture. We'll call out quorum placement in the SOW (controllers in racks A,C,E with dedicated out-of-band management network). Requirement: sub-2ms inter-controller latency; symmetric MTU recommended.

2) NVMe local PV eviction & ownership: Redwood will deliver a small reclaim-operator (declarative) that enforces eviction based on annotated PVs (label cache=true). Owner model: Redwood operates the operator and hands over runbook + automation to Riverton post-cutover. We'll include a 30-day elevated-runbook support option.

3) Compliance evidence (minimal set we will provide):
   - Network segmentation diagram + MTU/LACP config (blockstore-io-diagram.png)
   - KMS integration guide + attestation checklist (we support BYO-HSM; will include connection playbook)
   - CSI config with encryption at rest settings and snapshot policy proof-of-concept
   - SOW draft (high-level deliverables, timeline, support window) — Marissa will attach.

4) On-call & SLAs: proposed 30-day elevated support window (Mon-Fri 08:00–18:00 PDT) with 1-hour P1 response and runbook-driven remediation. Optional extended 24/7 support is available as a paid addon.

Workshop scheduling: Tue 15 Jun 10:00–12:00 PDT conflicts for us. We'll take Wed 16 Jun 13:00–14:30 PDT (90 minutes) — calendar invite sent: https://meet.google.com/xyz-abcq

Prework request (please fill before the workshop):
- rack & crossconnect spreadsheet (attached riverton-nodeclass-matrix.xlsx)
- switch model and NIC vendor + firmware versions
- initial RPS and 95p latency targets for each model endpoint

If procurement needs the SOW draft ahead of the workshop, Marissa will share the one-pager today.

Thanks and see you Wednesday,
Diego
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: riverton-nodeclass-matrix.xlsx (fill), site-intake-checklist.pdf
